speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the Government will review its investment mandates with GIC to consider the suggestion from some industry players for GIC to allocate part of its investments to securities listed on the Singapore Exchange to revitalise our local stock exchange.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: GIC must therefore continue to make professional investment decisions and the Government should not direct or interfere with GIC's investment decisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Second, to preserve the international purchasing power of the Reserves, especially for crisis needs, GIC invests in a globally diversified portfolio that reflects the availability and attractiveness of global investment opportunities and asset classes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Doing so will compromise our objectives for setting up GIC, which is not beneficial for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Under our current arrangements, GIC can already invest in appropriate Singapore companies if these companies have a global footprint and generate good returns to GIC's portfolio.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: In addition to anchoring international enterprises which bring new ideas, technology and good jobs, we will continue to groom and develop local companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Some of these companies will have the potential to list locally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Another priority is to help more companies which are listed on the SGX to grow their operations and expand into overseas markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: By becoming globally competitive and having a larger international presence, these companies would become more attractive to global investors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: We have implemented schemes to support business innovation, transformation and internationalisation to help Singapore-based companies develop their capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: We will continue to work with industry stakeholders on this goal.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I do agree with the Minister that we should not compromise on delivering returns and to achieve the best Net Investment Returns Contribution for the country.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But having said that, I would still nevertheless like to ask the Second Minister how our very own investment agencies like GIC, Temasek, the Monetary Authority of Singapore, can help strengthen our status as a premier international financial centre, given the scale that they have, as well as the sophistication in terms of the scope of investments.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think I would like to respond in two parts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First is to say that Singapore's financial sector, as a whole, is doing well.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The local equity market is, of course, one part of it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But Singapore continues to be an important pan-Asian gateway for capital formation and intermediation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this includes foreign exchange – we are the largest foreign exchange centre in Asia Pacific.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have almost US$1 trillion in foreign exchange traded daily in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Singapore is a developed pan-Asian asset management centre, with over 1,100 asset managers and over S$4.9 trillion of assets under management.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our bond market has grown significantly in recent years, reaching $512 billion in 2022, with foreign issuers making up half the issuance volumes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SGX is also one of the largest bond listing venues in Asia.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And, of course, a new area that we are going into, is sustainability.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are a leader in sustainable finance in the region, accounting for over 60% of cumulative sustainable bonds and loans issuance in ASEAN in 2022.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Having said that, we do recognise that for the local equity market, more can be done to grow this segment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are working closely with the industry to look at what is the best way to do this.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There are different ways to achieve this goal, including what I mentioned in my main reply: working with companies, grooming local companies that are able to go IPO and list here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Existing companies that are already listed on the SGX but helping them to grow their presence, to grow their operations because when you expand overseas, global investors, including institutional investors then become more interested in doing research and investing in this company, and I think that will help to increase the amount of activity and liquidity here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For the Government's investment entities, like Temasek, GIC, they do invest locally, but I think there is a difference between asking them to make those investment decisions based on returns and what is in the best interests for shareholders, for Singaporeans ultimately, versus we give them a directive to invest locally.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Given that a vibrant local equity market is an integral part of an innovative economy.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Over the last 20 years, actually, the equity markets in Singapore have been on a steady decline, in terms of the number of IPOs that have come onto the market, the liquidity and all that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, does the Government plan to have an integrated plan on reviving our local equity market?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there a plan that the Government has in mind?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is an important part of our overall economy.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It would not only help to support our local companies who want to list and expand.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It will also be an important contribution to our status as a financial centre.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I mentioned earlier in my response to Mr Liang, there are different ways to achieve this goal and some, I think, are more viable, more sustainable than others.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I think what we need is that the local equity market, in a way, there has not been an integrated effort to promote the market.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, now, I think we have reached a stage whereby I think we should be paying more attention to it.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, what I am asking is that, does the Government have a very definite integrated plan and does the Government feel the urgency now to give priority to promoting our local capital market?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think from what the Minister have said just now: you are doing this, you are doing that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I think there ought to be a new emphasis.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And I think a lot of the market participants have actually voiced these concerns to the Government for many years already.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I hope that there is no misunderstanding on that front.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not disagree with Mr Leong that this is something we want to do better.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But as I mentioned, there are different ways to achieve the goal.
